clue.text: Seen at a minor disturbance in Sicily

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters of the words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted at a small commotion somewhere on Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' rearranges the letters of AT A MINOR into the name of the Sicilian hill town.
explanation.definitionFit: Taormina is a resort town on the east coast of Sicily, so it is a place found on that island.

parts.note: trumpets are brass instruments; Whitehall is the London street of government ministries, whose senior officials are the high-ranking ones

explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government ministries; trumpets suggest an instrument section, but the phrase means the most senior officers or officials.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest-ranking officers and officials are known by this phrase, from the gold braid on their caps.

clue.text: While shepherds watched, the beanstalk grew !

definitions.text: While shepherds watched, the beanstalk grew !

parts.words: While shepherds watched, the beanstalk grew
parts.note: the carol's shepherds watched their flocks by night, and Jack's beanstalk shot up in a single night

explanation.walkthrough: The carol 'While shepherds watched their flocks by night' and Jack's beanstalk, which shot up between dusk and dawn, both point to the same span.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means during the night, or very suddenly, which suits both the carol's shepherds and Jack's magic beans.

clue.text: "The silence sank Like —— on my heart" (Coleridge)

definitions.text: "The silence sank Like —— on my heart" (Coleridge)

parts.words: "The silence sank Like —— on my heart" (Coleridge)
parts.note: fill the gap in a line of The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, comparing silence to sweet sound

explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner: 'The silence sank like music on my heart'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge likens the silence to harmonious sound, the melody that soothes the mariner.

parts.note: 26 across is the kindly carer of Spenser's poem, and rearing a child is what such a carer gives

explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 26 across is a carer who rears children; the upbringing such a carer gives is the answer here.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbringing or rearing is the training a child receives from those who look after it.

parts.note: read 'Cushy' as 'of Cush': in Genesis Cush fathered the mighty hunter before the Lord

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cushy' looks like slang for easy, but it means belonging to Cush, the biblical father of the great hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis 10 names this son of Cush as a mighty hunter, and his name has become a byword for any keen huntsman.

parts.note: 'gen' is British slang for information, so being wise about the gen means being informed

explanation.walkthrough: 'gen' is British forces slang for information; someone wise to the gen is well informed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well informed, with inside knowledge, is what someone wise about the current information is.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held and scanned: 'Roy turns to mechanically (5)'. ROBOT reads as ROB + TO reversed, but no clue word gives ROB (only Roy, as in Rob Roy) and 'mechanically' is an adverb for a noun; no honest parse.

clue.text: So many years wasted, we hear

indicators.note: tells the solver the word meaning wasted is to be said out loud and its sound written down

parts.note: something wasted away has decayed

explanation.surface: A speaker laments how many years have been thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals that DECAYED, from 'wasted', is spoken; it sounds like the ten-year span.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten years make up the span, so it is a set number of years.

clue.text: I got the shiny material in burnt indigo

parts.note: satin is a glossy woven fabric

explanation.surface: Someone acquires glossy fabric dyed a dark blue colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burnt indigo' looks like a colour for the fabric, but oxidising indigo yields this orange-red compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatin is the chemical made by oxidising the blue dye, so it is what the dye becomes when burnt.

clue.text: Palace accompaniments for nostalgic roaming vocalists

definitions.text: Palace accompaniments for nostalgic roaming vocalists

parts.words: Palace accompaniments for nostalgic roaming vocalists
parts.note: recalls the song Home, Sweet Home: 'Mid ... and palaces though we may roam', sung by homesick singers

explanation.walkthrough: The song Home, Sweet Home opens ''Mid pleasures and palaces though we may roam', so the answer goes with palaces for those singing it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song's first line the delights are paired with palaces, making them the palace's companions for roaming singers.

definitions.meaning: a brown shade the French name after tobacco leaf
the French tobacconist's shop, where smokers buy supplies

explanation.definitionFit: In French the word names a tobacco-brown shade, and it is also the tobacconist's shop where a smoker buys cigarettes.

clue.text: Such letters were used for spelling

definitions.text: Such letters were used for spelling

parts.words: Such letters were used for spelling
parts.note: the old Germanic alphabet's characters were carved for magic charms, so 'spelling' means casting spells

explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' suggests writing words letter by letter, but here it means casting spells: the old Norse letters were used in magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Characters of the ancient Germanic alphabet were carved as charms, so such letters served for magic spells.

clue.text: Waiting to be offered a drink ? It's only natural

definitions.text: Waiting to be offered a drink
definitions.meaning: not yet given a round by anybody, so still dry
describing material left raw, with no processing applied

explanation.definitionFit: Someone not yet bought a round has not been stood a drink, and a natural substance is one left unprocessed.

parts.note: the French word for wisdom, used in English for sound judgment

explanation.definitionFit: This is the French noun for wisdom or good sense, borrowed into English writing.

parts.note: sailors are 'salts', and their earthy humour is salty, tasting of brine

explanation.walkthrough: A sailor is an 'old salt', and racy humour is called salty, so sea-wit has a briny taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A briny taste is the flavour of seawater, and racy humour is also called salty.

parts.note: a papal envoy, sent by the Vatican as its ambassador to a foreign government

explanation.definitionFit: A papal ambassador is the Pope's diplomatic representative, carrying messages from the Holy See.

parts.note: 'Characteristic' hides 'character': writing in characters that stand for ideas, as in Chinese script

explanation.walkthrough: 'Characteristic' suggests typical, but it points to written characters, symbols that each stand for an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A written symbol representing an idea rather than a sound, as in Chinese script, is this kind of character.

parts.note: the proverb says fine plumage makes fine birds, so these suit birds well

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'fine feathers make fine birds' lies behind it: plumage is what makes birds look fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage covers birds, and the proverb says fine plumage makes fine birds.

definitions.meaning: distilling equipment produces whisky and other strong drink
single frames taken from a film, used as publicity pictures

explanation.definitionFit: Distilling apparatus is where alcoholic spirit is made, and single frames from a film are publicity photographs.

parts.note: the Roman god of sowing gave his name to the planet circled by famous rings

explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity of agriculture names the sixth planet, famous for the rings around it.

clue.text: Got by fast but ineffective workers?

definitions.text: Got by fast but ineffective workers?

parts.words: Got by fast but ineffective workers
parts.note: plays on the idiom 'getting ... fast', said of busy people who achieve nothing

explanation.walkthrough: Hard workers who achieve nothing are said to be 'getting nowhere fast'; that place is what such workers reach.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'getting nowhere fast' describes frantic effort without results, so this is the destination of quick but useless workers.

clue.text: Clerk to the first woman barrister

definitions.text: Clerk to the first woman barrister

parts.words: Clerk to the first woman barrister
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice Portia disguises herself as a lawyer, and her maid poses as her clerk

explanation.walkthrough: In The Merchant of Venice Portia argues in court disguised as a lawyer; her maid goes with her disguised as the clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: Portia's waiting-woman in Shakespeare dresses as a clerk to accompany her mistress in court.

clue.text: Let's have a chat and a drink

definitions.text: Let's have a chat and a drink

parts.words: Let's have a chat and a drink
parts.note: to mix socially, chatting; the word first meant drinking together

explanation.definitionFit: To socialise familiarly is the sense, and the word once meant to drink to each other.

parts.note: a patient discharged from hospital is out
a patient who is better is fitter

explanation.surface: A patient is sent home from hospital because he has recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a hospital discharge, but 'Providing he's' defines a supplier of clothes and equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplier of clothing and kit is someone whose trade is providing it for customers.

parts.note: Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel counts the men in a boat

explanation.walkthrough: Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel is titled for this many men in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure in Jerome's title Three Men in a Boat is a number of boatmen.

clue.text: Indicating the possibility of the use of force ?

definitions.meaning: the auxiliary verb used for what may happen
power, strength, as in 'with all one's ...'

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it shows that something may happen, and as a noun it means power or strength applied.

clue.text: The doctor with militant Irishmen finds the lady

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
the IRA, the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: A medical man accompanied by Irish rebels tracks down a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Moira is a woman's given name, so the clue's lady may bear it.

parts.note: quotes Spenser's Prothalamion: 'merry London, my most kindly ...', the city that raised him

explanation.walkthrough: In Prothalamion Edmund Spenser calls London, where he was born, 'my most kindly nurse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser's poem calls his native city the one who reared him, like a woman caring for a child.

clue.text: It's off to the country for an auburn shrew!

definitions.text: It's off to the country for an auburn shrew!

parts.words: It's off to the country for an auburn shrew
parts.note: an auburn shrew is a red-haired Kate, as in Shakespeare's Taming of the Shrew: 'Rusty Kate' runs together into the verb

explanation.walkthrough: The verb means to send someone to the country (or down from university); said quickly, 'Rusty Kate' is that verb, and Kate is Shakespeare's shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: To send away to the country, as a college sends a student down, is this verb's sense.

clue.text: "On some fond —— the parting soul relies" (Gray)

definitions.text: "On some fond —— the parting soul relies" (Gray)

parts.words: "On some fond —— the parting soul relies" (Gray)
parts.note: fill the gap in Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, the loving bosom a dying man leans on

explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Thomas Gray's Elegy: 'On some fond breast the parting soul relies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's dying man rests on a loving bosom, the chest of someone dear to him.

parts.note: the genteel ladies of Mrs Gaskell's Cranford went out in pattens on their feet and folding silk hoods on their heads

explanation.walkthrough: In Gaskell's novel Cranford the ladies walk out in pattens (raised overshoes) and folding hooped hoods.
explanation.definitionFit: These folding hooded bonnets were worn by early Victorian ladies over their caps, matching the pattens on their feet.
